title: Compose and file one letter at the end of an armed run
action: At the end of an armed run, compose the stored entries into one letter and file it (D4, D9). The body carries five sections — Done / Where I departed from the plan and why / Broken or unfinished / Needs your call / Next — and a section with nothing to report is dropped, never printed empty (D7). Composition may reorder, group and drop, and may never state a fact no stored entry carries (D8). Each Needs-your-call item carries a stable id naming what it blocks (D13). One letter maps to one run, never one night (D11). Render any departure through the existing deviation_text in verbs/knowledge/ rather than a second renderer (plan.md Discovery).

truths: An armed run that ends composes its entries into exactly one letter and files it (D4, D9).
The body carries the five D7 sections and a section with nothing to report is absent rather than empty.
Composition states no fact that no stored entry carries — it may reorder, group and drop only (D8).
Each Needs-your-call item carries a stable id and names what it blocks (D13).
Two runs in one night produce two letters, not one (D11).
An attended run records entries and files no letter (D9).
A run with zero entries is handled without producing an invalid letter.
Departures render through the existing deviation_text, not a second renderer.

acceptance: An armed run files exactly one letter per run with the five sections, empty ones dropped, no invented facts, stable ids on Needs-your-call items; an attended run files none; two runs in a night file two letters.
